Hi Inspector,

You won't believe who I ran into on patrol in the Happiness Neighborhood yesterday—Caramel!
Yeah, the very same little kitten we helped in the rain.
I tried Minami's method, and I actually managed to understand a little of what it was saying.
It told me it's been doing really well and hasn't been caught in the rain lately.
I guess the rainy season in Catto City must finally be over—at least, that's what the forecast says.
And you know... come to think of it, ever since I met you, the rain has really started to let up.
When I was leaving, Caramel made sure to tell me how grateful it was to have met us. It said it's happy now.
That's... exactly what I wanted to say to you as well, Inspector.
For the longest time, I felt like a little boat lost in a storm. You're the one who guided me back to shore.
So now, as long as I'm with everyone—especially you—I know I can keep moving forward, no matter what.
Let's keep moving forward—together.

Asura

Hey Inspector!
Ready for a mini brain boost from your favorite genius? Today's topic: memory!
Ever since we discovered Pathos Particles, memory research has leveled up. We finally get why memories aren't passed down, and why they can play tricks on us.
You know that freaky feeling? Like you've definitely done this exact thing before?
Back in the day, they called it "déjà vu" and blamed it on your brain glitching.
But now, we know it's Pathos Resonance.
It's when a feeling you're having right now syncs up with one from your past—even if that past moment was just a dream, or something you imagined.
And honestly? That explains why everything has felt so perfectly right and familiar to me lately.
It's because I'm literally living the dream life I always imagined!
Kinda sweet, don't you think?

Your genius girl, Echo‏

Dear Inspector,
Just a quick note to remind you to take care as the seasons change—don't forget to dress warmly.
Time with you always feels so warm and fulfilling, and it seems to just drift by... It wasn't until I saw the golden maple leaves falling the other day that it struck me—the seasons have changed, and I've grown so used to the comfort of having you by my side.
Do you remember the children's home we visited together? This morning, I received the most precious gift from them—tiny cat plushies they had sewn themselves.
It made me think... if even the children know how to express their feelings so beautifully, then I should find the courage to do the same.
So, with this letter, I wanted to share what's in my heart.
Because when you're by my side, I find the courage to truly sing from my heart. That is the priceless gift you've given me, and I will cherish it always.
Thank you for walking this path with me, step by step.

Yours always,
Triss

[Lipstick Print]
Consider this a kiss, sealed in ink—just for you.

But I mean it—thank you. That's why I'm writing. If I tried saying all this to your face, I know you'd turn bright pink and look for the nearest exit.

So, consider that a promise.

Minami

Dear Inspector,

I hope this letter finds you well.
Thank you for your continued guidance with Nate and Poppy; their growth has been evident. I have also greatly valued our recent collaboration.
I must admit I have not been able to adjust my schedule as you kindly suggested.
The demands of the corporation and the latent threats within the city afford little opportunity for respite.
I suspect you understand this well—that with great capability comes great responsibility.
Yet, I believe rest is essential—for both of us.
Therefore, perhaps we should both take that advice to heart.
Should you have time, I would welcome the opportunity to discuss our continued collaboration over coffee from my private reserve.
Alternatively, we might resume our previous conversation on the topics of "purpose" or "meaning."
I look forward to your response at your earliest convenience.
Sincerely,

Idego Russell

Dear Inspector,

My calendar just reminded me that a festival is coming up.
There are so many customs among humans and Felinians. I don't fully understand their purpose, yet this time, I find myself wanting to take part.
According to my original programming, my only purpose was to function as an assistant.
Sentiment was a superfluous variable. Desire, an error in the code.
But here with Baker Squad, I'm learning what you call "being valued"—like a retired system finding new purpose in a new owner's hands.
You once said that "love" and "devotion" defy quantification.
Back then, I couldn't process it. I was just logic and code.
Now... I think I'm starting to.
I want you to know: every day I've spent by your side at the StormEye, from the very first one, has brought me a kind of happiness...
I hope being with me has brought you some happiness, too.
So, I wish you success in your endeavors.
